test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What does the Finance Bill presented in the Budget mainly contain?

options.text: Proposals related to tax changes or rules

solution:
The correct answer is __**Proposals related to tax changes or rules**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Finance Bill** is introduced in the Parliament of India as part of the Union Budget process. It contains the government's proposals for the **amendment of tax laws** and other financial regulations.
 
• It primarily includes provisions related to **taxation policies**, such as changes in income tax, corporate tax, Goods and Services Tax (GST), customs, and excise duties.
 
• The Finance Bill is presented **annually** by the Finance Minister along with the Union Budget, as per **Article 110 of the Indian Constitution**, and must be passed by both Houses of Parliament.
 
• Unlike the Appropriation Bill, which deals with expenditure, the Finance Bill focuses on **revenue generation** methods for the government.
 
• Once the Finance Bill is passed and receives the President's assent, it becomes part of the law and implements the proposed tax changes for the upcoming financial year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Details of Government Borrowing Plans:**

 
 
• This refers to the government’s plans for raising funds to bridge the fiscal deficit through borrowing instruments like **government securities (G-Secs), treasury bills**, and external loans.
 
• These details are presented in the **Expenditure Budget** and not in the Finance Bill. Hence, this option is incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Estimates of State-Level Expenditure:**
 
 
• The Union Budget focuses on central government finances. State-level expenditures are prepared and presented separately by each state government in their respective budgets.
 
• Therefore, this aspect is not covered under the Finance Bill. Hence, this option is incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy Statements of RBI:**
 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is responsible for monetary policy, which includes managing interest rates, inflation, and liquidity in the economy.
 
• These statements are released periodically by the RBI and do not form part of the Finance Bill. Hence, this option is incorrect.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Types of Finance Bill:**

 
 
• **Finance Bill (Category 1):** Includes provisions related to taxation and other financial proposals. Requires approval as per Article 110 of the Constitution.
 
• **Finance Bill (Category 2):** Includes broader financial proposals that are not exclusively related to taxation. Requires approval as per the normal legislative process.
 
 
 
• **Special Features of the Finance Bill:**
 
 
• It is introduced as part of the budget presentation in the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• It must be passed within a period of **75 days** from its introduction in Parliament.
 
• The Finance Bill is a **Money Bill**, meaning that it requires approval from the Lok Sabha but not the Rajya Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Key Tax Components in the Finance Bill:**
 
 
• Income Tax Amendments: Adjustments in tax slabs, exemptions, and deductions.
 
• Corporate Tax Adjustments: Revisions in tax rates for businesses.
 
• Indirect Taxes: Changes in GST, customs, and excise duties.
